title: Introduction & First Vision

intro.heading: Who will you play?
intro.description: Practise a conversation aloud with a partner. It takes about 8–10 minutes, and your phone gives you prompts when you need them.

missionary.label: Mormon missionary
missionary.speaker: Missionary
missionary.description: Read the prepared lines aloud. You don’t need to invent any answers.

christian.label: Christian
christian.speaker: Christian
christian.description: Welcome your visitor and answer in your own words.

items.title: Why the accounts give different ages
Primary accounts of the First Vision
The Correct Name of the Church (October 2018)

opening.text: Hi! We’re missionaries from The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints. Do you have a few minutes to talk about our beliefs?
opening.caption: Introduction

help.prompt: Answer in your own words, or use this reply.
answers: Sure, I have a few minutes. I’m a Christian myself.

topics.title: Why did the naming guidance change?
topics.summary: The full Church name, and the earlier “I’m a Mormon” campaign.
topics.background: Church leaders now ask people to use the full name of the Church. Your partner may compare this with the earlier “I’m a Mormon” campaign. You only need to read your line.

question.text: You might know us as Mormons. We’re encouraged to use our full Church name because it includes Jesus Christ. We believe his Church should be called in his name.
question.caption: 3 Nephi 27:7–8 · Book of Mormon

help.hint: Remember the earlier “I’m a Mormon” campaign. Explain why the later guidance raises a question for you about the change.
answers: I remember the Church promoting “I’m a Mormon.” Later, President Nelson said leaving Jesus’ name out of the Church’s name was a victory for Satan. That change makes me wonder how the earlier campaign fits with the later teaching.
help.context: This passage supports explaining concerns respectfully. It is not evidence about the campaign itself.
help.note: The course uses this change to raise a question about guidance from Church leaders. It is more than a naming preference, but the change alone does not settle whether the Church’s religious claims are true.

topics.title: How many First Vision accounts are there?
topics.summary: Joseph Smith’s prayer, and the written accounts of his vision.
topics.background: Latter-day Saints teach that God the Father and Jesus Christ appeared to Joseph Smith in answer to his prayer. Your partner may mention the written accounts. You only need to read your line.

question.text: Joseph Smith said he prayed after reading James 1:5: “[If any of you lack wisdom, let him ask of God.](ref:james-1-2-6)” We believe God the Father and Jesus Christ appeared to him. We call this the First Vision.
question.caption: James 1:5 · KJV

help.hint: Recall the number of accounts and the explanation you might hear for their differences.
answers: I understand there are nine written accounts: four Joseph wrote or had someone write for him, and five written by people who heard him tell it. I also understand that the Church says the differences can fit together, much like differences between the four Gospels.
help.context: The Bible tells Christians to check claims about messages from God. This passage supports examining a claim. It does not, by itself, prove that the First Vision was true or false.
help.note: The course wants you to know both the number of accounts and the explanation commonly offered for their differences.

topics.title: Responding to the Gospel comparison
topics.summary: Comparing Joseph’s accounts with the four Gospels.
topics.background: This is one response you might hear about the different accounts. It is not what every Latter-day Saint will say. You only need to read your line.

question.text: The four Gospels don’t all include the same details about Jesus. We see Joseph’s accounts in a similar way. Different details can help give a fuller picture.
question.caption: Luke 1:1–4 · KJV

help.hint: Recognize the comparison, but explain why the specific differences still matter.
answers: I understand the comparison. Different details can sometimes fit together. But that doesn’t automatically explain every difference in Joseph’s accounts. We still need to look at what each one says.
help.context: Luke describes how he put his account together. This helps us discuss written accounts, but it does not settle whether Joseph’s accounts fit together.
help.note: The expected response in the course is that the accounts can be brought together into one consistent story. Recognizing that response helps you prepare a clear reply.

topics.title: Pointing to a specific difference
topics.summary: Why the accounts don’t all sound the same.
topics.background: The 1832 account has a scribe’s addition placing Joseph in his “sixteenth year,” which means age 15. Later accounts say about 14. The Church explains this as a difference in remembering the timing. You only need to read your line.

question.text: Joseph told the story at different times and to different people. We believe that helps explain why the accounts don’t all sound the same.
question.caption: Proverbs 18:13, 17 · KJV

help.hint: Use a specific example. The course points to the different ages given in the accounts.
answers: One difference that concerns me is his age. The 1832 account places him at 15, while later accounts say he was about 14. Saying the accounts focus on different details doesn’t fully explain that difference for me.
help.context: Listen carefully and consider more than one side before deciding.
help.note: The course suggests asking about Joseph’s age rather than only saying that the accounts differ. Here, that concern is written as a statement so the learner playing the missionary does not need to invent an answer.

evidence.heading: What do the accounts say?
evidence.text: A scribe added wording to the 1832 account placing Joseph in his “sixteenth year,” which means age 15. Later accounts place him at about 14.
evidence.context: The Church explains this as a difference in remembering the timing and notes that the age wording was added by a scribe. The course asks learners to consider whether that explanation is convincing.

topics.title: When someone hasn’t heard about the accounts
topics.summary: Pointing a friend to the accounts they can read.
topics.background: Speak as someone who knows only the usual First Vision story. You only need to read your line.

question.text: I know the usual First Vision story. I didn’t know there were other written accounts.
question.caption: Your turn · Lesson 1

help.hint: Explain that the accounts are available and provide a source they can read for themselves.
answers: The Church has published the different accounts and an explanation on its own website. I can show you where to find them. That way, you can read what each account says for yourself.
help.context: Be ready to explain what you know, gently and respectfully, as this passage describes.
help.note: The course recommends providing references, including the Church’s own material. Share the information without making someone feel embarrassed for not knowing.

reading.label: Read the accounts and the Church’s explanation

closing.text: Thanks for talking with me. I’ve enjoyed hearing what you think. Have a good evening!
closing.caption: Wrap up conversation

prompts: Which course point do you feel more ready to explain now?

items.label: 3 Nephi 27:7–8
items.context: Latter-day Saints cite these verses for calling the Church by Christ’s name. Reading them helps you understand why the naming guidance matters to them.

verses.text: Therefore, whatsoever ye shall do, ye shall do it in my name; therefore ye shall call the church in my name; and ye shall call upon the Father in my name that he will bless the church for my sake.

And how be it my church save it be called in my name? For if a church be called in Moses’ name then it be Moses’ church; or if it be called in the name of a man then it be the church of a man; but if it be called in my name then it is my church, if it so be that they are built upon my gospel.

items.label: James 1:2–6
items.context: James encourages believers facing trials to ask God for wisdom, in faith. Joseph Smith said verse 5 led him to pray.

verses.text: My brethren, count it all joy when ye fall into divers temptations;
Knowing this, that the trying of your faith worketh patience.
But let patience have her perfect work, that ye may be perfect and entire, wanting nothing.
If any of you lack wisdom, let him ask of God, that giveth to all men liberally, and upbraideth not; and it shall be given him.
But let him ask in faith, nothing wavering. For he that wavereth is like a wave of the sea driven with the wind and tossed.

items.label: 1 John 4:1–3
items.context: John tells believers not to accept every spirit, but to test whether a message is from God by what it confesses about Jesus Christ.

verses.text: Beloved, believe not every spirit, but try the spirits whether they are of God: because many false prophets are gone out into the world.
Hereby know ye the Spirit of God: Every spirit that confesseth that Jesus Christ is come in the flesh is of God:

And every spirit that confesseth not that Jesus Christ is come in the flesh is not of God: and this is that spirit of antichrist, whereof ye have heard that it should come; and even now already is it in the world.

items.label: Luke 1:1–4
items.context: Luke explains that he set out an orderly account, drawing on those who were eyewitnesses from the beginning, so that his reader could know the certainty of what he had been taught.

verses.text: Forasmuch as many have taken in hand to set forth in order a declaration of those things which are most surely believed among us,
Even as they delivered them unto us, which from the beginning were eyewitnesses, and ministers of the word;
It seemed good to me also, having had perfect understanding of all things from the very first, to write unto thee in order, most excellent Theophilus,
That thou mightest know the certainty of those things, wherein thou hast been instructed.

items.label: Proverbs 18:13–17
items.context: Verses 13 and 17 apply most directly: answering before hearing is folly, and the first to state a case seems right until someone examines it.

verses.text: He that answereth a matter before he heareth it, it is folly and shame unto him.
The spirit of a man will sustain his infirmity; but a wounded spirit who can bear?
The heart of the prudent getteth knowledge; and the ear of the wise seeketh knowledge.
A man’s gift maketh room for him, and bringeth him before great men.
He that is first in his own cause seemeth just; but his neighbour cometh and searcheth him.

items.label: 1 Peter 3:13–16
items.context: Peter tells believers to be ready to give a reason for their hope, with meekness and respect, and to keep a good conscience when others disagree.

verses.text: And who is he that will harm you, if ye be followers of that which is good?
But and if ye suffer for righteousness’ sake, happy are ye: and be not afraid of their terror, neither be troubled;
But sanctify the Lord God in your hearts: and be ready always to give an answer to every man that asketh you a reason of the hope that is in you with meekness and fear:
Having a good conscience; that, whereas they speak evil of you, as of evildoers, they may be ashamed that falsely accuse your good conversation in Christ.

sourceNotes: Lesson 1, from the supplied worksheet and answer key, in plain English. The five exchanges follow worksheet order and keep the course’s arguments: (1) the contrast between the “I’m a Mormon” campaign and President Nelson’s October 2018 teaching that removing the Lord’s name from the Church’s name is “a major victory for Satan” (The Correct Name of the Church; paraphrased, never as a claim that every use of “Mormon” is satanic); (2) nine documented accounts, four firsthand and five contemporary secondhand, and the comparison with the Gospels; (3) anticipating that the accounts can be brought into one story; (4) a specific concern about age: a scribe’s addition to the 1832 account places Joseph in his “sixteenth year” (age 15), later accounts say about 14 (First Vision Accounts FAQ, “Why do accounts… differ”); (5) pointing an unaware friend to Church-published accounts. Omitted as unverified: the answer key’s $6.1 million figure and the claim that the campaign ended the same year. The course’s “multiple first visions” question is a facilitator discussion approach only, not a historical conclusion and not a question back to the missionary. The Church History Museum is not promised; the online accounts are the resource offered. Christian answers never ask the missionary a question. Bible quotations are KJV; 3 Nephi 27:7–8 is labelled Book of Mormon. Scripture text checked against churchofjesuschrist.org. The wrap-up beat uses the app’s fixed closing id “closing” (the brief’s “wrap-up-conversation”).
